issue: tense: English is present throughout, but h₁ludʰét, l̥gʰént, sh₂ént are aorists with secondary endings ('arrived', 'lay down', 'became sated'); defensible as completive, but present-tense lines should take present forms
h₂óweyes-kʷe h₁éḱwos: -kʷe sits on the first conjunct; NP coordination is 'A B-kʷe' (h₂óweyes h₁éḱwos-kʷe)

h₂ur̥sdʰí: the zero grade of *h₂wers- is *h₂wr̥s-; here both the w and the r are vocalized (read h₂wr̥sdʰí; the engine's IMP.2SG cell is wrong at source); h₁éḱwōs-kʷe káprōs: -kʷe on the first conjunct (read h₁éḱwōs káprōs-kʷe)
wéwked: the root is *wekʷ- 'speak', so the reduplicated aorist is wéwkʷet (Ved. avocat, Gk. eipe); the labiovelar is missing. Also h₁estu is unaccented (h₁éstu)

tewóm h₃ókʷs: the neuter possessive is paired with an -s nominative; if 'eye' is neuter its nominative is bare h₃ókʷ (the engine lists both). The rest is good: perfect subjunctive leléykʷeti 'is missing', gʷémeti subjunctive in the 'if' clause, swā́s agreeing with fem. h₂ówins
h₃réḱs is a nominative (and short-voweled, against h₃rḗǵs elsewhere) used as the possessor 'king's'; this needs the genitive h₃rēǵés. Also súHnum: u-stem acc. sg. is suHnúm (Ved. sūnúm)
pl̥h₁éwbʰis: the instr. pl. of the u-stem should be zero-grade suffix + ending, *pl̥h₁ubʰís (Ved. purúbhis), not the engine's full-grade -éw-bʰis; h₂éboln̥s-kʷe wósh₂r̥: -kʷe on the first conjunct
kʷís ... h₂élomes: 'who nourishes' needs 3sg h₂életi; h₂élomes is 1pl 'we nourish'

póteyey lewbʰṓy bʰúHdʰi: the predicate 'dear' is put in the dative, agreeing with the husband ('become to the dear husband'); it should be nom. fem. lewbʰéh₂ agreeing with the daughter. Minor: suHnúes (nom. pl. *suHnéwes, Ved. sūnávas); bʰúHdʰi accent (bʰuHdʰí); dóh₃r̥ is a marginal lexeme beside déh₃rom/déh₃nom
polh₁ús-kʷe h₁sih₁ént: polh₁ús is nom. sg.; 'may they be many' needs nom. pl. polh₁éwes. Also gʷṓs-kʷe h₂ówins and káprons-kʷe h₁éḱwons put -kʷe on the first conjunct
polh₁ús-kʷe h₁sih₁ént: nom. sg. polh₁ús with a 3pl verb for 'may they be many'; needs polh₁éwes. ǵʰéys (secondary ending) for timeless 'you who drive away' is acceptable as an injunctive
h₂nḗr-kʷe gʷḗn: -kʷe on the first conjunct (read h₂nḗr gʷḗn-kʷe); the dual verb l̥gʰtā́m and dual tóh₁ are good
n̥th₂grṓs h₁sént: the referent ('they' = the ears of grain, h₂éḱōs, neuter pl.) needs neuter n̥th₂gréh₂ with a singular h₁ést under the corpus convention; masc. pl. + 3pl does not agree
puHróm-kʷe wósh₂r̥: -kʷe on the first conjunct (read puHróm wósh₂r̥-kʷe)

méǵh₂s ... h₁wésus h₁syéh₁s addresses Earth with masculine adjectives; *dʰéǵʰōm is feminine wherever it is animate (Gk. khthṓn, Ved. kṣā́s, Lith. žẽmė), so this should be fem. (méǵh₂ih₂ / h₁uséwih₂). The engine spec has gender m, which is wrong at source. Also -kʷe on the first conjunct in puHróm-kʷe h₂élbʰit, mélit-kʷe ǵʰutóm médʰu and méǵh₂s-ge-kʷe h₁wésus; dédh₃mes accent (weak stem *dedh₃més, Ved. dadmás)
gʷíh₃wom is PST.1SG 'I lived'; 'and they (the two cattle) lived' needs 3du gʷíh₃wetām (or 3pl gʷíh₃wont). Also ǵʰéslom gʷówes-kʷe ḱm̥tóm h₁éḱwōs: -kʷe on the first conjunct

tense: English is present but yéwgt, h₂wérst, h₂wékst, méwdt are aorists (past); h₂éryeti/h₂érye drop the root h₃ of *h₂erh₃- (h₂érh₃yeti), inconsistent with h₂érh₃trom in the same text; sóh₂wl̥-kʷe n̥bʰrós: -kʷe on the first conjunct
h₂élbʰitih₁ is nom./acc. DUAL ('two barleys'); the object 'the barley' needs acc. sg. h₂élbʰit

This is Schleicher's 1868 fable in pre-laryngeal, Sanskritized notation (a-vocalism, no laryngeals or palatals, akwabʰyams, wawakat, agantam); none of it is well-formed in the corpus's handbook notation. Keep it only as a labeled historical text, or replace it with a modern version (e.g. h₂ówis h₁éḱwoybʰos wéwkʷet ...)
h₂éǵrons is acc. PLURAL, but the English and the following singular h₁ím ('plough it') need acc. sg. h₂éǵrom. Minor: h₂érye lacks the root h₃ (h₂érh₃ye)
